verdicts.title: Structure in Communication Complexity and Constant-Cost Complexity Classes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Several theorems and conjectures in communication complexity state or speculate that the complexity of a matrix in a given communication model is controlled by a related analytic or algebraic matrix parameter, e.g., rank, sign-rank, discrepancy, etc. The forward direction is typically easy as the structural implications of small complexity often imply a bound on some matrix parameter. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a general survey of research directions linking communication complexity to matrix parameters like discrepancy and rank, without stating any specific bound on NW-design slice matrices of DISJ or the spectral discrepancy quantity ρ(f, D_n) defined in the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Near-optimal bounds on bounded-round quantum communication complexity of disjointness
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We prove a near optimal round-communication tradeoff for the two-party quantum communication complexity of disjointness. For protocols with $r$ rounds, we prove a lower bound of $\tildeΩ(n/r + r)$ on the communication required for computing disjointness of input size $n$, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns bounded-round quantum communication complexity of disjointness and quantum information complexity bounds via generalized discrepancy, not Nisan–Wigderson design-slice spectral discrepancy matrices for randomized DISJ. It neither asserts nor refutes the specific σ_max/m bound on NW-design slices conjectured.

verdicts.title: Multiparty Communication Complexity of Disjointness
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We obtain a lower bound of n^Omega(1) on the k-party randomized communication complexity of the Disjointness function in the `Number on the Forehead' model of multiparty communication when k is a constant. For k=o(loglog n), the bounds remain super-polylogarithmic i.e. (log n)^omega(1). The previous best lower bound for three players until recently was Omega(log n).

verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns multiparty Number-on-the-Forehead lower bounds for Disjointness via approximate polynomial degree techniques, not Nisan-Wigderson design-slice matrices or spectral/discrepancy bounds of the specific form ρ(DISJ_n, D_n) ≤ C·m^{−1/2} proposed in the conjecture.
